Sumanta Das, Angela Google, Ashley Buchanan, Christopher Lavan, Elaine Finan, John Stringer, Rachel DiCioccio This report provides highlights of the committee’s work through the 2024-25 academic year.
JCAPROA was formed in late Spring 2024.
The committee combines the previous Academic Program Review Committee and the Learning Outcomes Assessment Committee.

The charges to the committee are as follows: According to the University Manual at sections 5.84.10 – 5.84.14, this committee is responsible for: (1) developing policies for URI student learning outcomes assessment, data distribution, and measurement frequency at the university-wide level, with the Faculty Senate’s and the Provost’s approval; (2) developing an ongoing review of the learning outcomes assessment process, interpreting external expectations for university-wide learning outcomes assessment, including those of accreditation bodies, and facilitating internal communication across units regarding way of meeting those expectations, and (3) guiding the implementation and revision of the Academic Program Review process (sections 8.86.10 – 8.86.14) and serving as a resource to departments and programs being reviewed.
The committee shall also develop an ongoing review of the learning outcomes assessment process, interpret external expectations for university-wide learning outcomes assessment, including those of accreditation bodies and facilitate internal communication across units regarding ways of meeting those expectations.

In the beginning 3 months of the committees work which involves April-May, and September 2024, the committee deliberated on the scopes of the work and developing clarity around the charges.
Through such deliberations the committee developed the following goals and subsequent objectives to be pursued over a period of three years.
GOAL 1: SEAMLESS INTEGRATION OF THE ACADEMIC PROGRAM REVIEW AND THE LEARNING OUTCOMES ASSESSMENT PROCESS.
Objective 1: Revision of the learning outcome assessment process.
Action point 1: Reflection on the design of an ideal assessment process.
Action point 2: Determine appropriate revision of the process towards an ideal process.
Action point 3: Conduct appropriate revision of the process for its integration with APR.

Objective 2: Revision of the academic program review process for necessary integration of the learning outcomes assessment.
Action point 1: Reflect on the current program review process and identify scopes for improvements.
Action point 2: Reflect on ways to facilitate the integration of the learning outcomes assessment with academic program review.
Action point 3: Implement changes to the APR process for the integration of learning outcomes assessment.
GOAL 2: INCREASE TRANSPARENCY AND ACCESSIBILITY IN THE ACADEMIC PROGRAM REVIEW AND THE LEARNING OUTCOMES ASSESSMENT PROCESSES.
Objective 1: Increasing faculty, staff and student participation in APR and LOO processes.
Action point 1: Reflect on maximizing faculty, staff, and student participation in academic program review and outcomes assessment.
Action point 2: Implement the above in consultation with teams 1 and 2.
Objective 2: Content development and management (Notifications regarding program review/ JAPROA website management/FAQ document/Creating templates) Action point 1: Timely notification to relevant departments and programs for self-study.
Action point 2: Curate and update contents on JCAPROA website periodically.

Action point 3: Develop a FAQ document for program review and outcomes assessment.
Action point 4: Develop evaluation rubric for academic program review reports.
In fall 2024, the committee identified that the departments who were supposed to be notified for their APR in Spring 2024 were not in fact notified.
The committee deliberated to create an off-cycle timeline for the department who were disadvantaged.
The timeline was adopted unanimously by the committee.
Also, the committee offered a training/information session to respective department chairs on the APR process in December 2024.
In early Spring 2025, the committee sent out notifications to the departments who are going up for APR review.
The committee also offered training/information session on the APR process to the departments going up for review.

In Spring 2025, the major focus of the committee has been to develop a comprehensive handbook for the APR process. This is motivated by the fact that in the past departments who were going up for review struggled to find all the information about the process and the timeline in one place. In this effort, the committee reviewed APR handbooks from other esteemed institutions and decided to model URIs handbook after that of The Ohio State University. This handbook is being developed to compile all the process documents in one place and make necessary additions to the processes. In this effort, the committee adopted a division of labor approach and divided the entire committee into 4 sub-groups. A team leader was assigned to each team who led the effort for specific sections of the team. We are happy to report that we now have a good preliminary draft of the handbook that will soon be posted on a Brightspace repository and be made accessible to the departments going up for review. During fall 2024, the committee also updated the APR schedule that keeps track of the cycles of review for specific departments and programs. It has been a tremendous team effort and a functional joint committee with voluntary and enthusiastic participation from all.

Assessment reports are evaluated during an intensive 3-day summer retreat, following a 3-day trainingand norming session for faculty peer reviewers using faculty teams and a third level of oversight toreview reports.
Ten faculty served on peer review teams (2023) for the first round of review (Level 1);each reviewer then served as an independent reviewer (Level 2) for all reports providing oversight toensure consistency in the review and scoring process.
Scoring rubrics guide report review of assessmentreport templates (accredited, non-accredited, interim).

To meet expectations in reporting, allnon-accredited and accredited program reports are expected to achieve a score of “Satisfactory”.
Programs exceeding expectations are recognized for their excellence in assessment practice.
It isimportant to note that rubric scores assigned by peer reviewers reflect neither a judgment of instructorsnor the student learning results revealed during the assessment process, but rather, all scores reflect thelevel of achievement of programs in their effort to use best practices and processes to conductassessment in order to yield valuable results.
The results of outcomes assessment are intended strictlyfor use by academic programs for curricular or assessment process improvement.
The use of a peer review process and a rubric scoring tool provides the opportunity to identify facultyand programs undertaking best practices in learning outcomes assessment.
The recognition of excellencein reporting is currently available for non-accredited undergraduate and graduate programs.

This doesnot diminish the content nor effort of accredited programs to report, but reflects the streamlinedaccredited report template which requires summary content and metrics that are typically readilyavailable, rather than the reporting on a program of the authentic assessment of student learning.
Recognition is determined by the aggregate of item and domain level rubric scores which define criteriarelated to the strength of the assessment process used to investigate issues around student learning,engagement of faculty, and plans for responding to findings and proposing/implementing interventionsfor improvement as needed.
